sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
• Reference date: 2026-11-20 (KST) · run id 2026-11-20-event · mode event (incremental) · previous published run 2026-11-17-event (run no. 21) · previous monthly run 2026-11 (Source: run information injected by the workflow)
  • Reason: The news monitor detected 2 reports. ① The source for "Google chose Blue Origin New Glenn to launch its AI satellites in 2029" is the official Google blog (11/19). The monitor linked it to T1 (4Q26 earnings), but it is not an earnings event. It is a competitor's orbital compute and competing launch event, so it serves as background for C-2030-1, and the New Glenn schedule overlaps with T4. ② "Musk: should not receive additional compensation from the Tesla-SpaceX merger" is a remark from NYT DealBook (11/18). Because it is a CEO remark, it is listed only in the T6 candidate table. The rest of the due items (3 financing reports · T7 expected date · NSSL ceiling · Starshield · Samsung · catch·Vulcan) are either events covered by the unpublished 11/18 and 11/19 runs or echoes of events handled by earlier runs. Reports are subjects to verify, not grounds for judgment (Source: workflow-injected reason · state.run.reason)
  • Reference share price: $138.43 — close on 2026-11-19 (Thu), −3.53%, volume 119,613,373 shares, intraday range $135.50~$147.29 (Source: stockanalysis daily history, retrieved 2026-11-20 KST)
  • Scope: Cross-check of the Google announcement against its primary source · record of the DealBook remark · re-verification against original documents of facts from the unpublished 11/18 and 11/19 runs · update of price-dependent arithmetic values · restoration of the Mission Control data budget. Scenario figures and discount rates are not recalculated (Source: prompts/monthly_run.md)
Conclusion first: Google stated on its official blog that it will make the first dedicated large launch of its orbital compute satellites (Project Suncatcher) on Blue Origin New Glenn in 1Q 2029. It did not disclose the number of satellites or the amount, and did not mention SpaceX. The first prototype went up on a SpaceX rideshare (reported), and this announcement does not mean the loss of an existing SpaceX contract. Google is an AI compute customer of SpaceX (reported) and a shareholder, and this event also confirmed it as a competitor in orbital compute. Even so, C-2030-1 counts only SpaceX's own orbital data center revenue, so there is no input to the judgment layer. The DealBook remark is a statement of intent, so it was listed only in the candidate table. From the two unpublished runs, the following were re-verified against original documents and adopted. ① The start of sales of the lessor-side SPV bonds for the $40 billion financing (Bloomberg), and 7 tranches · $35.5 billion at 7.75% · 8.3% (Semafor). It is the same $40 billion, and it is not a fixed lease rate. ② The T7 ⓒ deadline passed without a public response. ③ Via the new route ⓕ, the Senate Foreign Relations Committee sent a letter directly to SpaceX (deadline 11/30). ④ The NSSL ceiling increase is not a contract award. Since no rule was triggered, the probabilities 30/50/20 · probability-weighted value $36 · band $36~$121 · center $68 are all unchanged, and the judgments on the 29 milestones are also unchanged. Against the reference price of $138.43, the center gap is −51% (Source: sections 1–5 below · state.probability_adjustment_rules).

1-3. Where it touches the judgment layer

  • Launch market: One dedicated heavy-lift launch went to a competitor. The amount was not disclosed, and as it is a 2029 matter it is outside the 12-month trigger window. There is no milestone or rule input (source: table 1-1 · state.probability_adjustment_rules).
  • New Glenn schedule: Amazon Leo has also reserved 24 New Glenn launches. The report that the return was pushed to 2027-01 is recorded in the T4 note (R5 is judged only on whether a plan launches at the end of 2027) (source: TNW, 2026-11-19 · state.triggers_next_12m[T4]).

sections.title: 3 Picking up the unpublished 11/18 and 11/19 runs — what was re-checked against the originals
sections.html:
A copy is not a source. This section lists only what this run re-opened and confirmed against the original text (source: _probe/unpublished/ · state.run.unpublished_runs).

3-1. $40 billion GPU financing — the lessor-side bonds (T5)
ItemBloomberg (11/17 09:53 EST)Semafor (11/18 07:53 EST)
ReportersCarpenter·Arroyo·SmithEllen DiMauro (exclusive)
StructureAn SPV run by Atlas SP, an Apollo affiliate, buys Nvidia chips and issues ABSSPV, 7 tranches
Size'Part' of the $40 billion — size of the part not givenTotal $40 billion · Apollo pre-funds about $20 billion, then sells down
Interest rateNone$35.5 billion at 8.3% and 7.75% · the risk tranche (under $3 billion in total) could exceed a blended 9%
Timing'as soon as this week''as early as this week'
Accounting wording'designed to keep the debt off SpaceX's balance sheet' · investment grade maintainedOff its own books
Source1 anonymous source · no SpaceX commentApollo declined to comment · SpaceX did not respond

(Sources: ⑤ Bloomberg (Yahoo-published version) · ⑥ Semafor)

  • Layer breakdown: The 10/26 8-K is a master finance lease commitment between the lessee (SpaceX) and the lessor. Principal is about $40 billion, and the fixed rate is set at pricing before signing. The reported SPV·ABS is how the lessor raises the money to buy the chips, so it sits at a different layer and does not contradict the 8-K (source: ① 8-K, 2026-10-26).
  • Interest rate: The SPV bond rate is the lessor's funding cost. Judging from the 8-K's rent structure (tranche financing cost 1/20 + fixed-rate interest), it could be close to the lease fixed rate. But no source text says they are the same. So it is not an input to proposed new rule ② (source: 8-K, 2026-10-26 · state.rule_proposals_not_applied).
  • 'Off-balance-sheet' wording: That the SPV bonds are not SpaceX's debt is a separate matter from whether SpaceX recognizes a lease liability. The determination is made in the first 10-Q after lease commencement (proposal ③) (source: state.rule_proposals_not_applied).
  • Judgment layer: Since it is the same $40 billion, the input to D-2027-1 (additional financing of $50 billion or less AND no equity raise) is unchanged. SPV bonds are not an issuance of SpaceX equity, so R3 does not apply either (source: state.milestones[D-2027-1]).
  • New developments: No report of pricing or closing was found in the 2026-11-20 KST search. There is also no 8-K for signing (source: EDGAR submissions, 2026-11-20 KST).
  • Not adopted: The expected ratings (Moody's A3 · KBRA A-), the CFO's remarks, and the 'about $4 billion bond' that a secondary summary relayed while citing Bloomberg. They are not in the published Bloomberg version, and no original text was found (source: state.run.unpublished_runs[2026-11-19-event].not_absorbed).

  • What the ⓕ letter requested: It asked that all records since 2026-09-01 be preserved. There are 3 questions. ① Who conveyed, approved or directed the restrictions after 10/1 (including whether direction came from outside SpaceX) ② An impact assessment and a chronology of restrictions and restorations ③ Who approved the restrictions now maintained or resumed and the one that recurred on 11/12. Both the preservation confirmation and the answers are due by 2026-11-30. The letter states 'To date, SpaceX has not provided any explanation or clarification of who authorized these restrictions' (source: Letter, original PDF, 2026-11-13).
  • Forecast check — wrong: The forecast was 'a response on 11/19 (KST) = ⓒ 11/18 + 1 day', but in fact the deadline passed with no response. There were two faulty premises. ① The deadline was read as 'the day a response comes'. A deadline is only 'the day one could come'. ② The searches in the 11/14–11/18 runs were aimed only at letters to government agencies, so the letter to SpaceX (ⓕ) was missed. Fix: No response is not counted as an event and is carried over to the next channel's deadline. The next checkpoint is ⓕ 11/30 + 1 day KST = 12/01 (monthly). When searching congressional channels, letters addressed to the company are included too (source: state.triggers_next_12m[T7].prev_2026_11_20).
